title: KPIRow
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow (two columns) or androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyRow with androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.snapping.rememberSnapFlingBehavior (one row that scrolls sideways), holding MonarchStatCard; MonarchInlineErrorRetry for a row that failed
summary: A recipe, not a component: the row of key figures at the top of a dashboard, made of MonarchStatCard in two columns, or in one row that scrolls sideways, with one loading and one error state for the whole row.
whenToUse: At the top of a dashboard or a report screen, for three to six headline figures that are read together, such as revenue, new customers and churn for this month.
whenNotToUse: For one figure, use MonarchStatCard on its own. For figures that each need a title, a menu and a body, use MonarchWidget in a grid. For a long table of figures, use a list with a detail screen.
api: FlowRow(modifier = Modifier.semantics { isTraversalGroup = true; contentDescription = label }, maxItemsInEachRow = 2, horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) { items.forEach { MonarchStatCard(label = …, value = …, modifier = Modifier.weight(1f), change = …, loading = loading) } }

LazyRow(state = state, flingBehavior = rememberSnapFlingBehavior(state), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3)) { items(items, key = { it.id }) { MonarchStatCard(…, modifier = Modifier.fillParentMaxWidth(0.7f)) } }

states.name: two columns
states.description: FlowRow with maxItemsInEachRow = 2 and Modifier.weight(1f) on each card: equal columns that wrap onto new rows. An odd last card takes the full width.

states.name: scroll
states.description: A LazyRow of cards at 70% of the width, so the next card peeks in, with snapping to each card. Use it for a hero row with many figures.

states.name: loading
states.description: Pass loading = true to every card; each shows its value placeholder and reads as loading. With no figures yet, show four placeholder cards labelled "Loading" in the app's language.

states.name: error
states.description: Replace the row with MonarchInlineErrorRetry in its Banner variant: the message, and Try again when the app can retry.

states.name: sizes and variants
states.description: Pass the same size (Sm for a dense row, Lg for a hero row) and variant (Card, or Plain inside a MonarchWidget) to every card.

appearance: Each figure is a MonarchStatCard: the card surface with its subtle border, the label in muted text, the value in the strong text style and the change in its success or danger color with a sign. The gaps are the theme's space3. The same roles change in dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web KPIRow is a component over StatCardGroup with an automatic CSS grid (columns, minItemWidth) and overflow = wrap or scroll. On a phone there is no room for an automatic grid of many columns, so on Android, as planned, it is a recipe: two equal columns (FlowRow) or one row that scrolls sideways with snapping (LazyRow, the pattern of a home screen's tiles). For three or more columns on a tablet, read currentWindowAdaptiveInfo() and raise maxItemsInEachRow. The web's whole-row loading and error props become loading = true on each card and MonarchInlineErrorRetry in place of the row; Monarch ships no strings for the recipe, so the app supplies "Loading" and the group label in its language. The web makes the scrolling row a tab stop; on Android a LazyRow scrolls with swipes and TalkBack's scroll actions. There is no iOS entry for this id.
accessibility: Each figure is one MonarchStatCard, read as one TalkBack element with its label, value and change; the change is also a sign and words, never color alone.
The row is a traversal group with the app's label ("This month"), so the figures are read together.
A scrolling LazyRow exposes TalkBack's scroll forward and backward actions.
A loading card reads its loading state instead of a value; the error banner's Try again is a button with a 48dp touch target.
edgeCases: An odd number of figures in two columns leaves the last card alone on its row at the full width; pass an even number or accept the wide card.
At font scale 2.0 the cards grow taller and the values wrap; the two-column layout keeps working down to a 320dp screen.
A LazyRow cannot sit inside another LazyRow; inside a vertically scrolling screen a LazyRow is fine because it scrolls the other way.
Keys: give each figure a stable id so a scrolling row keeps its position when values update.

examples.title: Headline figures with changes
examples.template:
FlowRow(
    modifier = Modifier.semantics {
        isTraversalGroup = true
        contentDescription = {{label}}
    },
    maxItemsInEachRow = 2,
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3),
    verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3),
) {
    MonarchStatCard(
        label = {{items.0.label}},
        value = {{items.0.value|double}},
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        format = MonarchMetricFormat.{{items.0.format|pascal}},
        change = MonarchMetricChange(
            value = {{items.0.change|double}},
            comparison = {{items.0.caption}},
            goodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.{{items.0.goodDirection|pascal}},
        ),
    )
    MonarchStatCard(
        label = {{items.1.label}},
        value = {{items.1.value|double}},
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        format = MonarchMetricFormat.{{items.1.format|pascal}},
        change = MonarchMetricChange(value = {{items.1.change|double}}),
    )
    MonarchStatCard(
        label = {{items.2.label}},
        value = {{items.2.value|double}},
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        unit = {{items.2.unit}},
        change = MonarchMetricChange(
            value = {{items.2.change|double}},
            goodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.{{items.2.goodDirection|pascal}},
        ),
    )
    MonarchStatCard(
        label = {{items.3.label}},
        value = {{items.3.value}},
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        hint = {{items.3.hint}},
    )
}
examples.code:
FlowRow(
    modifier = Modifier.semantics {
        isTraversalGroup = true
        contentDescription = "Last 30 days"
    },
    maxItemsInEachRow = 2,
    horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3),
    verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(MonarchTheme.spacing.space3),
) {
    MonarchStatCard(
        label = "Open tickets",
        value = 128.0,
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        format = MonarchMetricFormat.Number,
        change = MonarchMetricChange(
            value = 0.12,
            comparison = "vs previous 30 days",
            goodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.Down,
        ),
    )
    MonarchStatCard(
        label = "Within target",
        value = 0.94,
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        format = MonarchMetricFormat.Percent,
        change = MonarchMetricChange(value = 0.02),
    )
    MonarchStatCard(
        label = "First reply",
        value = 42.0,
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        unit = "min",
        change = MonarchMetricChange(
            value = -0.08,
            goodDirection = MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection.Down,
        ),
    )
    MonarchStatCard(
        label = "Satisfaction",
        value = null,
        modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
        hint = "No survey answers yet",
    )
}
